creator: pourandplate
title: Agua de Jamaica
description: Deep red, tart, barely sweet. Twelve minutes of steeping and not a minute more.
steps: Bring half the water to the boil with the cinnamon stick.
Take it off the heat, add the hibiscus, and steep for 12 minutes.
Steep it any longer and it turns tannic and drying.
Strain, pressing the flowers gently, and stir the sugar in while it is hot.
Add the remaining water cold and chill thoroughly.
Sharpen with lime juice and serve over a lot of ice.

creator: pourandplate
title: Horchata
description: Strain it twice through cloth. Once leaves it gritty and gritty horchata is not worth drinking.
steps: Soak the rice, almonds and cinnamon in the water overnight at room temperature.
Blend the whole lot, soaking water included, for a full two minutes.
Strain through a fine cloth, squeezing hard to get everything through.
Strain a second time; the texture is the entire point of the drink.
Stir in the sugar, vanilla and remaining water.
Chill hard and stir again before pouring, as it settles.

creator: pourandplate
title: Watermelon Agua Fresca
description: Strain it and cut it with water. Neat watermelon puree is thick and cloying after two mouthfuls.
steps: Blend the watermelon on its own until completely liquid.
Strain it through a sieve to take out the pulp, pressing it through with a ladle.
Stir in the cold water — it should be a drink, not a puree.
Add lime juice, then sugar only if the melon needs it.
Chill for an hour so it is properly cold rather than iced down.
Serve over ice with mint slapped between your palms first.

creator: pourandplate
title: Thai Iced Tea
description: Cool it before it meets ice, and float the evaporated milk. Half of this drink is how it looks in the glass.
steps: Boil the water and steep the tea hard for 5 minutes.
Strain it twice through a fine sieve or a tea sock.
Stir the sugar and condensed milk into the hot tea until dissolved.
Cool it completely before it goes near ice, or it will taste watered down.
Fill tall glasses with ice and pour the tea over.
Float the evaporated milk on top and let the drinker stir it in.

creator: pourandplate
title: Turkish Coffee
description: Cold water, low heat, and never let it boil. The foam is the measure of whether you got it right.
steps: Measure the cold water with the cup you will drink from.
Stir the coffee, sugar and cardamom into the cold water in the cezve.
Heat it very slowly over a low flame without stirring again.
When the foam rises to the rim, pull it off — do not let it boil over.
Spoon some foam into each cup, return the pot to the heat, and let it rise once more.
Pour slowly and let it stand a minute for the grounds to settle.

creator: pourandplate
title: Flat White
description: Three seconds of stretch, no more. A flat white is a cappuccino that knew when to stop.
steps: Pull a double ristretto into a warmed 6oz cup.
Start with cold milk in a cold jug; it gives you longer to work.
Steam with the tip just under the surface for 3 seconds only, then submerge it.
Take it to 140F — hot enough to drink, not hot enough to scald the sugars.
Swirl and tap the jug until the surface is glossy with no visible bubbles.
Pour from high to break through, then drop low and close for the pattern.

creator: pourandplate
title: Bubble Tea
description: Pearls are made and drunk the same hour. Refrigerate them and they go hard and chalky.
steps: Boil the pearls in plenty of water for 20 minutes, then leave them covered off the heat for 10.
Drain and steep them in the brown sugar with a splash of hot water.
Brew the tea strong in the remaining water and cool it completely.
Spoon the pearls and their syrup into the bottom of tall glasses.
Add ice, then the cold tea, then the milk so it marbles down through.
Use a wide straw and serve at once; the pearls harden as they sit.

creator: pourandplate
title: Patatas Bravas
description: Boil, dry, then fry. The drying step is the one everybody skips and the one that decides it.
steps: Simmer the potato cubes in salted water for 8 minutes, then drain and dry them thoroughly.
Let them steam dry in the colander for 10 minutes; wet potato will never crisp.
Fry the garlic, add the paprika and cayenne off the heat, then the tomatoes and vinegar.
Simmer the sauce for 20 minutes and blend it smooth.
Fry the potatoes in hot oil until deep brown and properly crisp.
Salt them immediately and spoon the warm sauce over just before serving.

creator: pourandplate
title: Gambas al Ajillo
description: Ninety seconds a side. The oil is half the dish, so keep bread nearby.
steps: Dry the prawns thoroughly and salt them 10 minutes ahead.
Start the garlic and chilli in cold oil in a shallow earthenware dish or small pan.
Bring it up slowly until the garlic is pale gold and the oil is fragrant.
Raise the heat, add the prawns, and cook 90 seconds a side — no longer.
Off the heat, stir in the paprika, vinegar and parsley.
Serve bubbling, with bread for the oil.

creator: pourandplate
title: Padrón Peppers
description: A very hot pan and more salt than feels right. One pepper in ten is hot, which is the game.
steps: Dry the peppers completely; any water will spit in the oil.
Get the pan as hot as it will go before the oil goes in.
Add the peppers in one layer and leave them alone for 2 minutes.
Toss once and cook another 2 minutes, until blistered and collapsing.
Tip onto a plate and salt heavily while they are still glossy.
Eat with your fingers, by the stalk.

creator: pourandplate
title: Croquetas de Jamón
description: The mix has to be properly cold before you shape it. Four hours is a minimum, overnight is better.
steps: Melt the butter, stir in the flour, and cook it for 3 minutes until it smells of biscuit.
Add the warm milk a ladle at a time, beating until each addition is completely smooth.
Cook the bechamel for 10 minutes until it pulls cleanly away from the pan.
Stir in the ham and nutmeg, spread it in a tray, and refrigerate at least 4 hours.
Roll the cold mixture into cylinders, then through egg and breadcrumbs.
Fry at 350F for 2 minutes until deep gold; the inside should be almost liquid.

creator: pourandplate
title: Arancini
description: Cold risotto or nothing. The cheese in the middle should pull when you break one open.
steps: Use risotto that has been refrigerated overnight; warm rice will not hold.
Stir the parmesan through the cold rice.
Take a golf ball of rice, flatten it, put a cube of mozzarella in, and close it around.
Roll each ball through flour, then egg, then breadcrumbs.
Chill the coated balls for 20 minutes so the crust sets.
Fry at 350F for 4 minutes until deep gold, and drain on a rack rather than paper.

creator: pourandplate
title: Calamari Fritti
description: Ninety seconds. Squid is tender under two minutes or after forty; there is nothing in between.
steps: Soak the squid rings in the milk for 20 minutes; it tenderises and helps the flour stick.
Mix the semolina and plain flour with the salt.
Lift the squid straight from the milk into the flour and toss hard.
Shake off every loose speck of flour before it goes in the oil.
Fry at 375F for 90 seconds only — past two minutes it turns to rubber.
Drain on a rack, salt at once, and serve with lemon.

creator: pourandplate
title: Edamame with Sea Salt
description: Salt the water like the sea, and salt them again hot. The pods carry the salt, not the beans.
steps: Bring a large pan of heavily salted water to a hard boil.
Drop the frozen pods straight in and cook for 4 minutes.
Drain but do not rinse; the residual heat dries them.
Toss while steaming with the sesame oil so the salt has something to hold to.
Add the flaky salt and toss again.
Serve hot with an empty bowl for the pods.

creator: pourandplate
title: Chicken Satay
description: Weave the meat onto the skewer so it cooks evenly. Speared straight through, the middle stays raw.
steps: Marinate the chicken in half the coconut milk with the turmeric and coriander for an hour.
Thread onto soaked skewers, weaving rather than spearing straight through.
For the sauce, warm the rest of the coconut milk with the peanut butter, soy and sugar.
Simmer it 5 minutes until it thickens, then sharpen with lime.
Grill the skewers over high heat for 3 minutes a side, basting with the marinade.
Serve with the sauce warm, not hot from the pan.

creator: pourandplate
title: Vietnamese Summer Rolls
description: Two seconds in the water. Any longer and it tears while you are still filling it.
steps: Have everything cut and laid out before you wet the first wrapper.
Dip a wrapper in warm water for 2 seconds only — it keeps softening on the board.
Lay the prawn halves cut side down first; they will show through the finished roll.
Add noodles, herbs, carrot and lettuce in a line across the lower third.
Fold the bottom up, fold the sides in, then roll tightly away from you.
Whisk the hoisin and peanut butter with a splash of water and serve alongside.

creator: pourandplate
title: Onion Bhaji
description: The onions make their own water. Add liquid too early and you get a batter ball, not a bhaji.
steps: Salt the sliced onions and leave them 15 minutes; they release the water that binds the batter.
Add the gram flour, spices, chilli and coriander straight onto the wet onions.
Mix with your hands, adding water a teaspoon at a time only if it will not come together.
The batter should barely coat the onion, not drown it.
Drop rough spoonfuls into oil at 350F and fry for 4 minutes until dark gold.
Drain on a rack and salt again while hot.

creator: pourandplate
title: Beef Empanadas
description: Cold filling, sealed edges. Warm filling steams the pastry and the seam bursts in the oven.
steps: Cook the onion slowly in the oil for 12 minutes until completely soft.
Add the beef, paprika and cumin and cook until browned, then season well.
Chill the filling completely; warm filling makes the pastry go slack.
Fold in the chopped boiled egg and olives.
Spoon onto the discs, wet the rim, fold over and crimp with a fork or a repulgue.
Brush with beaten egg and bake at 400F for 22 minutes until deep gold.

creator: pourandplate
title: Vegetable Samosa
description: A stiff dough and a low fryer. Hot oil browns the outside long before the pastry has cooked.
steps: Rub the 4 tbsp oil into the flour until it holds together when squeezed, then add water to a stiff dough.
Rest the dough for 30 minutes under a cloth.
Fry the cumin and coriander seeds, add the potato, peas, chilli and garam masala, and cool completely.
Roll the dough thin, cut into semicircles, and form cones with a wet seam.
Fill, press the top edge firmly closed, and check for gaps.
Fry at 325F — lower than you think — for 8 minutes, so the pastry cooks through and blisters.

creator: pourandplate
title: Pan con Tomate
description: Grated tomato, not chopped. The pulp soaks in; diced tomato just sits there and rolls off.
steps: Toast or griddle the bread until it is dry and crisp right through.
Rub the cut garlic over the hot surface, lightly — it is a seasoning, not a topping.
Grate the tomato halves on a box grater, skin side out, and discard the skins.
Spoon the tomato pulp over the bread and let it soak in for a moment.
Pour olive oil over generously and finish with flaky salt.
Eat straight away, standing up, before the bread softens.
